## Overview

The scalar reference compilers for an `axiolid-model` geometry graph.
`ReferenceMeshCompiler` walks the graph and produces one `TriMesh` per root:
it resolves instances and collections, composes transforms, tessellates
profiles, sweeps, B-reps and authored meshes, and hands booleans to whichever
`MeshBoolean` provider it is given. `ReferenceExactCompiler` compiles the
families it supports to exact B-reps, places instances under rigid
transforms, cuts placed openings from placed extrusions with the general
exact boolean, clips them by half-spaces through the same boolean, and
refuses the rest by name. This crate
owns graph traversal and dispatch; the construction algorithms themselves
(profile flattening, extrusion, revolution, sweeps) belong to
`axiolid-construct`.

## Design notes

- The caller always supplies the tolerance through `ExecutionOptions`;
  there is no built-in default. Without an explicit chord budget, curves are
  flattened to the linear tolerance.
- Read volume through `CompileOutcome::solid_mesh`: a surface model can
  compile to a closed mesh without bounding a solid.
  A mesh is reported `MeshClosure::Solid` only when it is a closed,
  consistently wound two-manifold; a declared solid that tessellates open
  is `MeshClosure::OpenSolid`, and `solid_mesh` refuses it.
- Before a mesh boolean, operand coordinates a rounding residue from the
  other operand's axis-aligned faces (16 `f64::EPSILON` of the operands'
  largest coordinate, about `2e-8` at georeferenced coordinates) are set
  onto them exactly, so a tool a rounding error short of its host's face
  leaves no skin that thin (#276); a thicker skin is authored and kept
  whatever the tolerance (#291). The move is at most the tolerance, none
  at zero, and the deviation report names it
  (`deviation::SNAPPED_OPERANDS`). A boolean whose snapped operands are
  refused is cut as given, with no snap reported.

## Changes

Latest release, 0.3.22 (2026-10-12):

### Added

- Run stations snap onto seams within their windows (#301, ADR 0082
  amendment): `SectionsAtStations` and `OpenSectionsAtStations` sections
  and the stations of the new `CurveRelation::OffsetsAtStations` (compiled
  as a sweep directrix and as a station basis, like `OffsetByStations`)
  are each snapped by the #294 rule (`station::window`, the oriented
  station's own) before the run is read, and the run stands on the snapped
  distances; a window holding two seams or straddled by one is refused by
  name, and snapped stations that no longer increase strictly are refused
  as `InvalidInput`. An interior station snapped onto a joint where the
  tangent turns is the mitre's knot, its section the mitre section whatever
  side it names; the run's first and last stations keep their outgoing and
  incoming readings; an interior station on a seam whose tangents agree (a
  roll jump) is placed in the frame of the side it names. Window `0` and
  `Outgoing`, the defaults, are today's reading.

### Changed

- `station::curve_path` documents that its pieces stay stated, each with
  the length the kernel measures, and that a caller without the graph who
  leaves the same pieces' ends open (#298) reads the same path (checked
  bitwise for an offset of a B-spline). Its output is unchanged.
